Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of a line segment and an arc of a semi-circle centered at $(4,0)$ with radius $2.$ Find the value of 
${\int }_{-2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$

${\int }_{-2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-2,2]$ and the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [2,6].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,2].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot 4 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [2,6].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =2+2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
